findings.detail: ck_l2f2_authority_phase permits only 'PHASE_A', so a Phase-B execution authority row cannot be recorded, and experiments.l2f2_resolve_claimed_execution resolves with a hardcoded a.phase = 'PHASE_A'. A materialized Phase-B job fails at claim time with "plan ... has no PHASE_A L2-F2 execution authority". 0011 states the intent explicitly: 'the ONLY phase 0011 admits. A later phase is a later migration, never a looser CHECK.'
findings.remedy_requires_authorization: a migration widening the runner boundary plus an administrative Phase-B authority preparation path
findings.title: migration 0011 admits only PHASE_A execution authorities

findings.action_taken: recorded, not adjusted — the rule is frozen and errs in the safe direction
findings.consequence: Phase B spends its full 480-job ceiling; racing yields no budget saving at this batch count.
findings.detail: with 5 of 10 members observed the frozen -1.0 * failure_rate term moves both bounds by exactly 0.5, so the worst reachable optimistic bound and the best reachable pessimistic bound are both -0.25. Elimination requires a strict inequality, so no candidate can be eliminated after one balanced batch.
findings.title: the batch-0 race can never eliminate a candidate

findings.detail: the observation reader and the expansion boundary selected every job in the database and refused the first unrecognised row. Correct while Phase A was the only plan; wrong the instant Phase B is persisted, because Phase-B executions would have entered Phase-A statistics.
findings.fix: one shared plan-scoped reading core (minos_engine.baseline.plan_observations) scoped by plan_hash. Narrows what is read; relaxes nothing about what a row must prove — a forged job claiming a plan hash still fails closed.
findings.title: Phase-A readers counted rows globally
